text:
anna: Heads up — noticed a tail-latency regression on Mistral-7B after the runtime patch that changed kernel ranking heuristics. Happening on sliding-window long conversations (seq ~1500-3000).
sam: When did you first see it? Any repro steps?
anna: Started ~2123440000 in prod canary. Quick repro locally:
```
./bench_gen --model m7b --seq 1800 --kv-warmup 1 --profile
```
Log snippet shows kernel selector switching to `matmul_small_kv` for some requests and latency spikes:
```
[2026-03-18T09:02:12Z] kernel_select: matmul_small_kv reason=tile_fit:false kv_bytes=51248 seq=1800
[2026-03-18T09:02:12Z] fallback: matmul_generic reason=latency_est>p50
```
sam: matmul_small_kv used to be faster for short seqs. If seq=1800 it's surprising. Could be kv_bytes calc or tile boundary logic.
jules: fwiw we changed batcher split logic last week: heuristics.batch_split_threshold lowered to 64 -> could cause more fragmented batches and worse KV memcpy behavior. Did you correlate with batch size?
anna: yes — observed many micro-batches of size 1 that cause excessive KV copy and kernel churn. Profiler output:
```
kernel_time(ms): matmul_small_kv=4.8, matmul_generic=8.1, kv_copy=6.9
per_token(ms): 0.012
observed_tail_p95: 310ms -> 720ms
```
mike: That kv_copy=6.9 looks bad. Is that host<->device memcpy or intra-gpu memmove due to packing?
anna: It's device memmove during KV tile compaction. The new rope scaling (we applied 1.25x) increases padded KV length, pushing some requests over tile boundaries. When that happens the kernel chooser prefers the 'small' kernel because it thinks matmul will be cheaper on smaller tiles, but we pay for the compaction cost.
sam: So rope_scale indirectly triggers a different kernel plus memmove. Nice catch.
jules: Two paths: 1) tweak batcher so fewer tiny micro-batches for long-convo workloads; 2) teach kernel selector to consider kv_compaction_cost estimate. Short-term we can force kernel override for m7b in canary.
mike: I can run a canary with forced kernel flag. What override syntax?
anna: config patch to console->model_overrides:
```
model_overrides:
  m7b:
    kernel_preference: [matmul_large_cache, matmul_generic]
```
That forces avoiding matmul_small_kv.
sam: Also consider increasing heuristics.batch_split_threshold to 96 for canary.
jules: Longer term: update kernel_cost_estimator to add `compaction_bytes` term. Rough pseudo:
```
estimated_cost = run_time(kernel, seq) + alpha * compaction_bytes / bw
```
We should add a micro-benchmark sweep: seq=[256,512,1024,1536,2048,3072], kv_bytes bins, and measure compaction and kernel switch overhead.
mike: I'll run the sweep on canary infra today and post numbers.
anna: FYI the regression affects m7b much more than 8x7b. On 8x7b head_dim/kv packing keeps tiles aligned even with rope_scale. 7b's kv_stride is smaller so rope_scale pushes it across tile boundaries more often.
sam: Good to capture in the model profile metadata: add kv_tile_stride, head_dim, rope_scale to model_catalog so selector can reason.
anna: Attached quick repro script and target numbers:
```
# run repro
for s in 1024 1536 2048; do ./bench_gen --model m7b --seq $s --profile > out_$s.log; done
# expected p95 before fix ~320ms, after override ~340ms, current ~710ms
```
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: rolling-canary/runtime-kernel-override -> 2123460000
mike: canary results: forcing matmul_large_cache dropped p95 from 710ms -> 360ms for seq=1800. kv_copy dropped to 1.2ms.
jules: nice. we'll follow up: (1) add compaction term to cost model (2) microbench sweep to auto-tune batch_split_threshold (3) add model metadata kv_tile_stride
anna: I'll open PR with the override and a test that simulates rope_scale >1.0 to prevent regression. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
sam: Can you add a short note in the release notes so oncall knows the temporary override exists?
anna: will do. :memo:
mike: adding results to perf-dashboard
jules: leaving this thread — follow-ups in the PR. :rocket:
